name: John Deere Precision Essentials: bundled precision agriculture technology
title: John Deere Precision Essentials: bundled precision agriculture technology
answer: John Deere's Precision Essentials page describes a bundled precision agriculture package combining display hardware, a StarFire 7500 receiver and a JDLink modem with renewable software licences, starting at $2,650. The most useful detail for anyone tracking automation in farming is the licence tiering: the Advanced licence is where guidance and automation features such as AutoTrac Implement Guidance, AutoTrac Turn Automation, AutoPath and Machine Sync sit, while the entry Essentials licence covers only AutoTrac, Section Control and RowSense.

sections.body: This is a product page published by John Deere on deere.com, describing its Precision Essentials bundled precision agriculture technology packages. It covers the hardware, software licences and pricing that make up the bundle, and it is written for prospective buyers configuring a machine rather than for a technical audience. The page was read on 4 October 2026 and no publication or revision date is stated in the text.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Precision Essentials is sold as one technology package at one upfront price, combining hardware, software licences and support. The hardware options are the G5 or G5Plus Display, the StarFire 7500 Receiver and the JDLink M or R Modem, which connects machines and transfers field data wirelessly. Buyers then choose a renewable software licence. The Essentials licence includes AutoTrac, Section Control and RowSense and requires a one-year term. The Essentials and SF-RTK licence adds SF-RTK to that set, also on a one-year term. The Advanced licence is the automation tier: it includes AutoTrac Implement Guidance, AutoTrac Turn Automation, AutoPath, In-Field Data Sharing, Machine Sync, Satellite Maps, Grain Harvest Weight Sharing and SF-RTK, again with a one-year licence required. The G5 series displays are described as offering 35% more screen space, three times faster processing and 1080p HD resolution. The StarFire 7500 with SF-RTK is said to deliver RTK-like accuracy within 2.5 cm, pull in up to 73% faster than SF3, and act as a drop-in replacement for the StarFire 6000 in integrated or universal form. JDLink Boost adds satellite connectivity to hold a connection under heavy canopies or where cell coverage is poor. The John Deere Operations Center connects data from fields, machines, operators and advisors for monitoring and analysis.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the Precision Essentials program starts at $2,650 for all three components. It gives the StarFire 7500 Receiver as achieving repeatable accuracy of plus or minus 2.5 cm, and says the StarFire 7500 with SF-RTK provides RTK-like accuracy within 2.5 cm and up to 73% faster pull-in times than SF3. The G5 series displays are credited with 35% more screen space, three times faster processing and 1080p HD resolution. Each of the three licence options, Essentials, Essentials and SF-RTK, and Advanced, requires a one-year licence.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in agriculture, this page is useful as a commercial reference point rather than a research document. It shows how automation capability is packaged and sold today: the Advanced licence is the tier that carries guidance and machine coordination features such as AutoTrac Implement Guidance, AutoTrac Turn Automation, AutoPath and Machine Sync, while the entry tier covers only steering, section control and row sensing. The accuracy and connectivity specifications, including 2.5 cm repeatable accuracy and satellite backup through JDLink Boost, indicate the sensing and positioning baseline that higher level autonomy depends on. The Operations Center description also shows field, machine and operator data being gathered in one place for monitoring and analysis.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: This is a commercial product page, so it presents John Deere's own offering and pricing without independent testing or comparison with competitors. It does not describe the algorithms, models or data processing behind the listed features, and it does not report deployment numbers, field results or research findings. The page is undated, and the pricing and licence terms given may change. It covers only the Precision Essentials bundle, not the wider John Deere product line.
